💡 Key Findings from Your Train vs. Val Audit

1. Train Flipped Anatomy

In Train (74 frames), inverted frames come primarily from Patient 20 (29 frames), Patient 12 (20 frames), and Patient 53 (5 frames). Surgical graspers clamp the visceral flap and gallbladder, hoisting the anterior ridge up to $Y \in [0.000, 0.170]$.

2. Val Flipped Anatomy

In Val (19 frames), Patient 40 (15 frames) exhibits identical severe dual-grasper retraction with the ridge elevated to $Y = 0.005 - 0.015$, accompanied by Patient 32 (4 frames) with lateral elevation.

3. Why Vanilla Models Failed

Because $92\%$ of Train is flat canonical dome views, standard models overfit to "Ridge is at the bottom". Your Junction Steering mechanism is what allowed Experiment 5 to achieve 70.91% on Patient 40 by anchoring predictions to the biological junction graph.
